propAHistory.note: 2026 tax bill not yet published in user series (left blank, unverified); +2.0% matches BOE LTA 2026/002 factor 1.02.
Implies ~1.1636% ad valorem (~$6,280) + ~$930 fixed parcel/special assessments.
Verified: BOE 2021-22 CCPI factor was 1.01036 (+1.036%, below 2% cap).
Flagged minor anomaly: total tax flat 2019→2020 despite +2% assessment (bond rate dip offset base increase).
Flagged minor anomaly: total tax flat 2017→2018 despite +2% assessment (voter GO bond levy offset).

propBHistory.note: SF FY25-26 rate UNVERIFIED; FY26-27 rate 1.18162182% (verified). Fixed parcel taxes/fees UNVERIFIED.
Matches BOE 2.0% cap; SF GO bond & parcel assessment adjustment.
Verified +1.036% BOE factor; -5.9% total bill drop reflects SF GO bond/parcel tax expiration.

paths.name: P1 · Sell Property A Same Year → Lump-Sum 70/30 Portfolio (Keep & Live in B)
paths.liquidity_status: High — immediate cash covers any Form 706 estate tax + reserves
paths.reinvestment_risk: High entry-valuation / crash risk (1929/2008 drawdown -35% to -60% if unphased)

paths.name: P2 · Sell Property A → 30m 3M–2Y Treasuries → 12m Equity Phase-In
paths.liquidity_status: Highest — sovereign 3M–2Y Treasury ladder (CA state-tax-exempt)
paths.reinvestment_risk: Moderate rate-rollover risk (-$54k/yr on $3M if yields drop 4.3%→2.5%), but cuts 1929/2008 trough loss by 55%+

paths.name: P3 · Occupy Property A Long-Term (Prop 19) + Lease All 3 Units of Property B
paths.liquidity_status: Constrained if estate > exclusion; 2-building landlord workload
paths.reinvestment_risk: Low market-entry risk; high single-region Bay Area real-estate concentration

paths.name: P4 · Rent Out Property A (Reassessed at FMV) + Continue Living in Property B
paths.short: Rent A (No Prop 19) + Live in B
paths.liquidity_status: Tightest — full reassessed Cupertino tax (~1.164% of FMV) compresses net yield to ~1.1%–1.7%
paths.reinvestment_risk: Low cash-deployment risk, but suspended passive losses (IRC §469) & low cap rate drag compounding

paths.name: M1 · Occupy Property A 3 Yrs (Prop 19) → Sell with IRC §121 ($250k/$500k) → Phased IPS
paths.liquidity_status: Delayed 3 yrs; caution — BOE LTA 2026/026 removes Prop 19 upon move-out (do not file if short-term only)
paths.reinvestment_risk: Deferred 3 yrs + 24m T-Bill buffer; shields up to $500k MFJ post-DOD gain via §121

paths.name: M2 · Rent Property A 5 Yrs (27.5-Yr MACRS) → Sell (25% §1250 Recapture + CA 13.3%) → Portfolio
paths.liquidity_status: 5-yr illiquid hold; triggers §1250 depreciation recapture + CA ordinary gain unless §1031 exchanged
paths.reinvestment_risk: 5-yr delayed equity entry + tax friction on post-DOD appreciation & recapture

paths.name: M3 · Occupy Property A (Prop 19) + Sell Property B (1/3 §121 + 2/3 Taxable, Exit SF Rent Control)
paths.short: Mixed: Live in A + Sell SF B
paths.liquidity_status: High — exits SF 3-unit maintenance & before SF $5M 2.25% transfer-tax cliff, but forfeits $114k Prop 13 base & pays capital gains on B
paths.reinvestment_risk: Moderate — smaller net proceeds than selling A because Property B has no step-up in basis

blackSwanRegimes.name: 1929–1938 Great Depression Crash Entry
blackSwanRegimes.desc: Inheriting & selling right at the late-1929 peak (-83% cumulative nominal equity crash by 1932; deflationary Treasury preservation).

blackSwanRegimes.name: 2008–2017 Global Financial Crisis Entry
blackSwanRegimes.desc: Inheriting & selling at start of 2008 GFC (-37.0% equity drop in Year 1; Fed cuts short yields from ~3.5% to near 0%, testing reinvestment risk alongside crash protection).

blackSwanRegimes.name: 1973–1982 Oil Shock & Stagflation Regime
blackSwanRegimes.desc: Back-to-back -14.7% and -26.5% equity drops with 7%–13% inflation; high short T-Bill yields & California Prop 13 2% assessment cap shine.

blackSwanRegimes.name: 2000–2009 Silicon Valley Dot-Com + GFC Lost Decade
blackSwanRegimes.desc: Three consecutive equity down years (2000–2002) followed by 2008 GFC — critical stress test for Silicon Valley concentration & lump-sum stock entry.

blackSwanRegimes.name: Normal / Bull Expansion Counterfactual (Reinvestment-Risk Check)
blackSwanRegimes.desc: Shows the OTHER side of the coin: if no crash occurs and 3M–2Y yields fall from 4.4% to 2.4%, parking 24–36m in Treasuries creates ~$180k–$310k of cash-drag opportunity cost.
